column1: # Named English dates and guarded contextual years. See docs/english-dates.md.
# Input aliases are matched using ASCII lowercase; dots are grammar punctuation.
# Reading policy. calendar and cardinal are the only accepted style values.
# Only contextual bare-year detection is restricted by these limits.
# A bare four-digit value is not a date without a preceding contextual cue.
# Determiners, prepositions and interval words also introduce a year; a
# following quantity noun (date_year_quantity) still keeps the cardinal.
# A bare year between matching marks is the citation shape: ( 1965 ) and
# "Press , 1992 .". The value lists the closing marks, and $ allows the end of
# the text. The quantity noun and the year range still decide, so
# ( 1965 copies ) and "scores were 1200 , 1400 and 1600 ." stay cardinals.
# A colon after a four-digit number is the timeline shape: "1830 : The first
# Constitution". The year range and the quantity noun still decide.
# A following quantity noun blocks the contextual-year interpretation.
# Generic segmenter continuation hints keep date candidates intact.
# Streaming boundary words for the new year cues.
# A second endpoint continues an interval whose first endpoint is a year.
# A decade is read as a plural year: 1960s nineteen sixties, 1900s nineteen
# A decade is more specific than the generic "digits with a tail" fallback.
